title: Browser Playback Auth Transport
problem: Media Web needs a secure browser playback transport because normal media element requests cannot attach bearer Authorization headers.
gates: cd apps/admin-web && npm run check && npm run test && npm run build

evidence.summary: Accepted short-lived browser playback tickets as the first browser media transport and recorded the decision in ADR 0036 after comparing cookie/session auth and JavaScript HLS/MSE with headers.

Added protocol-owned browser playback ticket request/response DTOs, Public Client OpenAPI route POST /sources/{source_id}/playback/browser-ticket, Rust and TypeScript client methods, and generated SDK coverage for browser-safe URL envelopes without raw locators or bearer-token media URLs.

Implemented opaque in-memory browser playback ticket issuance and validation in nako-server for direct stream, remux, HLS playlist, and HLS segment routes, including expiry, source/mode scope, Library Access rechecks, Range preservation, HLS segment ticketing, and redaction-safe errors/debug output.

Wired Media Web watch pages to request browser playback tickets through the Public Client data source and render an HTML5 player from browser-safe URL envelopes without exposing bearer tokens, raw Source Locators, raw stream paths, or ticket values in visible UI text.

Wired Media Web watch player events to User Playback State writes through the Public Client data source with start gating, 30-second playback-position throttling, pause flushes, selected-source payloads, and end-of-play watched behavior.

continue_policy.notes: Run BPAT-060 closeout. Verify final backend/frontend gates, record browser smoke, and close or split follow-ons for desktop native playback, subtitles, advanced codec/HDR capability mapping, credential/session UX, and account/admin roles.
